title: No More Deaths on Canal: Emergency Rally and Vigil

location.venue: Manhattan Bridge Colonnade Plaza in front of Canal and Chrystie Street
address_lines: We will meet up in the plaza across the Popeyes at Canal and Chrystie Street.

description:
This past weekend, two New Yorkers were horrifically killed by a speeding driver exiting the Manhattan Bridge.

On Wednesday, we will stand together to demand safer streets and an end to traffic deaths on Canal Street. While City Hall fails to prioritize safety, more New Yorkers die avoidable deaths. 

We will stand together with family, friends and neighbors of Kevin Cruikshank, and we will also honor and acknowledge the tragic passing of May Kwok.

Canal Street is one of the most dangerous streets in Manhattan, and is a DOT designated senior priority corridor under Vision Zero. We cannot stand by while the City continues to let pedestrians and cyclists die or get seriously injured. The community has fought for a redesign for years. The time is now to Fix Canal Street.

Join us for a rally telling Mayor Adams we need safety NOW, and for a vigil honoring those whose lives were taken on Canal Street this past weekend.


Meetup Location: 

The rally will take place at the Manhattan Bridge Colonnade at the Canal and Chrystie Street Plaza. 

Easiest access is to begin at the Popeyes at 125 Canal Street, and cross the street to the plaza (SW of the street.) 

We will have wayfinding posters and crossing guards to help with access and safety.

*** 

上个周末，两位纽约人被一名高速驶出曼哈顿大桥的司机撞死，场面十分惨烈。

这周三，我们要团结一致地站出来，要求更安全的街道，结束Canal街上的交通死亡。市政府迟迟不把安全当回事，更多人因此死于本可以避免的悲剧。

我们会与Kevin Cruikshank的家人、朋友和邻居站在一起，缅怀并悼念May Kwok的不幸离世。

Canal街是曼哈顿最危险的街道之一，同时也是市交通局在“零死亡愿景”下指定的重点老年人安全通道。我们不能再袖手旁观，任由市政府继续忽视行人和骑车人的生命安全。社区多年来一直呼吁进行道路重新设计。现在，是时候修复Canal街了。

加入我们的集会，一同向市长亚当斯呼吁：我们现在就需要安全措施！同时，我们将举行烛光悼念仪式，缅怀上周末失去生命的逝者。

集会将在曼哈顿大桥柱廊广场举行，地点位于Canal街与Chrystie街交汇处的广场。
最方便的路线是从Canal街125号的Popeyes 炸鸡店出发，穿过马路前往广场（位于街道西南角）。我们会有海报出示和引导员，方便大家顺利通行、安全到达。

*** 

上個週末，兩位紐約人被一名高速駛出曼哈頓大橋的司機撞死，場面十分慘烈。

title: Meet and Greet - Dr. Bryan Hambley

description:
Please come and meet Dr. Bryan Hambley, CANDIDATE for Ohio Secretary of State --because Ohio needs a democracy that delivers for our communities. We will be hosting Dr. Hambley on Wednesday, August 20 at 6:00 PM at the Metzenbaum Center, 8200 Cedar Road, Chesterland, OH 44026.  Come and hear what the candidate has to say and Dr. Hambley will be staying after to answer questions you may have.

MORE ABOUT DR. HAMBLEY:
Bryan grew up on a small family farm in a tight-knit community where he saw the impact of people coming together. When he was a child, the state tried to shut down his town’s small public school. The town of 800 people got into their trucks, drove to the state capitol, and made their voices heard to save the school, the heart of their community. His parents taught him this was democracy at its best: a community rallying to do together what no one could do alone. 

Ever since, Bryan has committed his life to fighting for what’s right. He has organized communities around key issues. 

Fighting against pharmaceutical companies using their money to buy influence in hospitals. 

Bringing critical health care to underserved communities. 

Standing up for the right to vote and be heard. 

As a cancer doctor who cares for leukemia patients, Bryan has helped hundreds of patients and families as part of a team of dedicated nurses, nurse practitioners, pharmacists, and physicians. In that time, he’s seen how outrageous healthcare costs are bankrupting families, health insurance denials are delaying urgent chemotherapy, and rural hospitals and nursing homes are closing and leaving communities without quality care. And yet, Ohio’s government has been silent on these and other vital issues. A rigged and unresponsive legislature prioritizes politicians over citizens. Bryan is running because caring for his patients and his community cannot end at the hospital door.

The people of Ohio deserve better. When Ohio’s Secretary of State used misleading ballot language in 2024 to confuse voters and maintain unfair districts, Bryan organized medical professionals across the state to fight back. He took his two young children door to door to talk with neighbors about how gerrymandering leads to an unresponsive and ineffective government. These conversations confirmed that Ohioans all want the same thing: a state government that works for the people. 

His wife, best friend, and partner, Jana, is a trauma surgeon, and together they have two wonderful children– ages 5 and 7. They are teaching their children the same commitment to democracy and to fighting for what is right that Bryan learned from his parents. 

Bryan is running for Secretary of State because he has seen how his patients and our communities suffer from a broken and gerrymandered democracy. He is passionate about making our democracy work. But, he cannot do this without you; Ohio needs a community of people working together to care for Ohio, and strengthen our state.

title: Bell County for Flood Infrastructure and Fair Maps: Rally & Testify

address_lines: Capitol Rotunda (inside, past the security checkpoint)

description:
Make your voice heard: No redistricting! Join us on Thursday at the Capitol (or online). We need to show just how many of us there are. That we're watching this legislative special session. And that we're demanding action from our elected representatives.

We say NO to further gerrymandering — it’s plain to see that the only aim of redistricting is to disenfranchise voters of color in Texas. The special session should focus solely on providing relief for flood victims and prevention of future devastation. 

HERE'S THE PLAN

12 P.M. // MEET UP IN THE ROTUNDA: Find us at noon on Thurs., July 24. We’ll be inside the Texas State Capitol Rotunda, past the security checkpoint at the entrance to the Capitol.

12:30 P.M. // RALLY IN THE CAPITOL: Demonstrate at the rally inside the Capitol, hosted by Texas AFL-CIO: https://www.mobilize.us/txaflcio/event/817526/

2 P.M. ONWARD // ATTEND THE REDISTRICTING HEARING: The exact timing for public testimony at the redistricting hearing is still TBA. In any case, you will have a few options (scroll down for detailed guidance):

. . . GOOD: Leave public comment online.

. . . BETTER: Come early on 7/24 to leave a comment in person at the Capitol kiosk.

. . . BEST: Join us to pack the Capitol on Thursday afternoon, and offer testimony or support others who are testifying.


PROVIDING PUBLIC TESTIMONY AT THE TEXAS CAPITOL

OPTION 1: ATTEND THE HEARING // If you’re attending the hearing in person, here are some guidelines to consider:

. . . PREPARE YOUR TESTIMONY: Whether or not you hope to speak in the hearing (or just support and listen), if you’re visiting the capitol you should draft a short letter with your views! The basic message we’re organizing behind is this: The special session needs to serve Texans. What Texans need right now is (1) aid for flood victims and their communities today and (2) infrastructure to alert us to flood dangers and prevent such devastation in the future. What we don’t need? New unfair maps that disenfranchise black and brown voters.

. . . PRINT YOUR TESTIMONY: After you draft your testimony, print 3 or more copies. You’ll have one to hold onto, and one each for your senator and representative. 

. . . CHOOSE YOUR ATTIRE: Business or business casual attire is appropriate. To present a united front, we’re going to distribute green ribbons to wear around our wrists. Green represents advocacy for flood victims and investment in flood infrastructure.

. . . KIDS ARE WELCOME: Children are welcome at the Capitol! They can even give testimony. Do be sure to bring plenty of water, snacks, and activities — it could be a very long day.

For more detail on giving public comment at the Capitol, check out this incredibly handy guide: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MCbvxemix8Dsv5MOjD-Vs-VAlZZzfvuPXZuLx8n8j9c/edit?tab=t.0

OPTION 2: SWING BY THE CAPITOL TO DROP OFF FEEDBACK, THEN LEAVE: If you aren’t able to join us all afternoon, another option is bring your prepared testimony and drop it off.

OPTION 3: IF YOU CAN’T MAKE IT TO AUSTIN, APPLY TO LEAVE VIRTUAL TESTIMONY: If you aren’t able to come at all, you can apply to leave virtual testimony: https://comments.house.texas.gov/home?c=c055. 


LOGISTICS

KEEPING IN TOUCH: After you RSVP, you’ll be invited to a GroupMe chat where you can ask questions, coordinate carpooling, and keep up with event-day communications.

PARKING: The Capitol Visitor Parking Garage (1201 San Jacinto Blvd., Austin, TX) is ideal. If garages are full, there is metered street parking in the blocks surrounding the Capitol. See the Capitol parking map for more information: https://tspb.texas.gov/plan/maps/doc/capitol_complex_parking_map.pdf

CARPOOLING: We strongly advise coordinating rides with others! After you RSVP, you’ll be invited to a GroupMe chat where you can ask questions, coordinate carpooling, and keep up with event-day communications.

WHAT TO BRING: Please bring a water bottle, any travel-friendly snacks you may need to get you through a long afternoon, and, most importantly: your public testimony! Whether or not you hope to speak in the hearing, draft a short letter with your views. Then, print 3 or more copies (one for you to hold onto, and one each for your senator and representative).

Please reach out if you have any questions! We look forward to getting down to Austin and holding our government accountable to the will and needs of the people with you!
